target: Faults mapped by the sponsor's experts that are absent from the USGS Quaternary + INGENIOUS catalogue used as labels.
ranking_basis: expected HOLDOUT-DTI improvement per unit implementation cost, then measured

hypotheses.name: Strike-conditioned structural corridor (SSCC)
layers: lidar_scarp_features_u8.tif (ex_max, ex_mean, step_max, lapneg_max, lappos_max, downface_max, upface_max, cross_max, relief, coh100)
hypotheses.physical_signature: Multi-scale scarp/curvature relief (0.1-5 km) with consistent strike continuity, supported by radiometric contrast and an independent structural map, i.e. the criteria a fault expert applies when drawing a trace.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: The detector is fitted to recover *withheld whole fault components* from geophysical evidence alone (the blind variant excludes every catalogue-proximity feature), so it can fire on a trace that no catalogue contains. Absolute elevation is deliberately excluded; only relief texture and shape are used.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: Earlier lanes placed sparse dots on single-scale ridge/curvature maxima or closed topographic gaps with hand-set rules. This lane learns a continuous corridor field from a supervised multi-layer model, uses a rank-cut operating point chosen on the pooled DTI curve, and emits ~266k cells rather than ~37k dots.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Bedrock ridge crests, landslide head scarps and fluvial terrace edges also produce steep, coherent short-wavelength relief; alluvial fan constructional surfaces can produce radiometric boundaries.
hypotheses.cost: medium (no new external data; 4 spatial folds x 200 s)

hypotheses.name: Radiometric K-Th disequilibrium alteration corridor
hypotheses.physical_signature: Along-strike K enrichment with Th depletion (low Th/K) caused by hydrothermal K-metasomatism / illite-adularia alteration above fracture conduits.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: Alteration halos extend hundreds of metres beyond mapped traces and mark active conduits; faults under alluvium have no scarp but can still carry a radiometric signature.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: The sites' 'scarp-radiometric-fusion' lanes fused radiometrics with topography as an edge term; this hypothesis targets a *ratio disequilibrium* directional signature and is not implemented here.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Playa/lacustrine clays and evaporites (high K, low Th), rhyolitic ash and agricultural dust; also vegetation-dependent U mobility.
hypotheses.cost: low-medium (needs only bands already cached, plus careful surrogate masking)

hypotheses.name: Magnetic-lineament continuity under cover (upward-continued TMI)
layers: official training_features.tif magnetics once login data is available
hypotheses.physical_signature: Upward continuation suppresses shallow volcanic noise and reveals deep basement lineaments; faults cutting magnetite-bearing basement appear as narrow gradient ridges that do not depend on topography.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: Faults buried under basin fill have no topographic expression, so catalogue maps built from surface geology can miss them entirely.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: Only one magnetic product (TMI upward-continued to 150 m) is cached; a full RTP/vertical-derivative/euler stack needs the organizer 19-band file (login) - no lane in this repo has used the upward-continuation geometry as its primary detector.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Lithological contacts, basalt flow margins and intrusive bodies produce the same narrow gradient ridges.
hypotheses.cost: medium (needs the organizer training_features.tif, which requires an authenticated download)

hypotheses.name: Geothermal-discharge-weighted structural linkage
hypotheses.physical_signature: Hot springs and high geothermometry cluster at fault intersections and relay zones; the prediction is the along-strike continuation and the step-over between two discharge sites.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: A spring pins a permeable structure, but the mapped fault trace commonly stops short of it; the continuation is exactly what is missing from the catalogue.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: A 'thermal-pop' lane already scored 0.1894 (user-reported) using thermal evidence as a density prior; this version conditions on the *pairwise geometry* of discharge sites and is not implemented here.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Evaporite-brine discharge, magmatic heat without faulting, and agricultural wells.

hypotheses.name: Multi-scale relief-texture entropy of the lidar surface
hypotheses.physical_signature: Fault-controlled topography has a characteristic band-limited roughness that is scale-invariant, so a local entropy/variance ratio separates it from smooth fans and from single-scale landforms.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: It is blind to any catalogue and to the sign of the scarp, so it can fire on an unmapped trace in either fault-polarity setting.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: No lane in this repository used a texture-entropy statistic; existing scarp lanes use first/second derivatives only.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Drainage networks, bedrock-ridge fields and landslide complexes all raise texture entropy.
